newsitem.title: USA: Bell Atlantic ordered to cut Maryland rates.
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic ordered to cut Maryland rates.

text.p: Bell Atlantic Corp. said Tuesday that the Maryland Public Service Commission ordered a $32 million rate cut, but agreed to adopt regulation that caps Bell Atlantic-Maryland's prices rather than its earnings.
"We are pleased that the commission has moved Maryland toward open telecommunications markets," said Daniel Whelan, president and chief executive of Bell Atlantic- Maryland.
"However, we are disappointed that the commission ignored the realities of the marketplace and required us to reduce rates by $32 million," he said.

Whelan's comments followed the commission's decision to apply the rate reductions to access charges that the long-distance carriers pay to Bell Atlantic to complete calls through the company's local telephone network.
In a separate order, the commission set a wholesale discount rate of 20 percent for companies reselling Bell Atlantic's local service to customers, Bell Atlantic said.
The commission set interim rates for unbundled network services that can be purchased on a piecemeal basis by competitors, Bell Atlantic said.
